title: Koshari
description: Rice, lentils, and pasta layered under a sharp tomato sauce, cumin vinegar, and a heap of fried onions. Egypt's national dish and the best argument for carbohydrate on carbohydrate.
notes: Every component can be made ahead. Assemble only at the table — the fried onions go soft within minutes of meeting the sauce.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onions in the neutral oil over a steady medium heat until deep brown and crisp, then drain on paper.
steps.tip: They go from brown to burnt fast at the end. Pull them a shade early — they darken on the paper.

steps.text: Keep a few spoonfuls of the onion oil back for the lentils.
Simmer the brown lentils in plenty of water until tender but still holding shape, then drain.
Cook the rice in the reserved onion oil and water until done, and boil the pasta separately.
Fry the garlic briefly, add the tomato passata, cumin, chilli flakes, and white vinegar, and simmer until thickened.
Layer rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas in a wide dish.
Pour the hot sauce over and finish with a generous pile of crispy onions.
